previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of renal transplant, hypertension, dyslipidemia, and moderate aortic stenosis was admitted for progressive dyspnea on exertion and atypical chest pain. Workup included a dobutamine stress echo, which was limited, and a low-probability VQ scan, ruling out pulmonary embolism. She underwent elective left and right heart catheterization, which revealed two-vessel coronary artery disease with a 70% stenosis in the mid OM2 branch of the circumflex artery. A bare metal stent was successfully placed. Hemodynamics showed moderately elevated left-sided filling pressures and moderate aortic stenosis. Lisinopril was uptitrated to 10 mg daily, and clopidogrel was initiated for dual antiplatelet therapy. Her transplant medications were continued without change. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans in cardiology and transplant clinics.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/oF with CKD ___ congenital ureteral disease s/p renal 
transplant x 2 (___) with humoral rejection in ___ 
(new baseline Cr 2.7-3.0), CAD s/p BMS on ___, with acute 
renal failure, kidney biospy suggestive of progression of 
progressive CKD.  Admitted to renal transplant service.

Patient's renal failure was thought to be multifactorial 
secondary to dehydration (poor po), contrast nephropathy, 
medication effect (ACEI and immunosuppressants), humoral 
rejection, BK virus, or progression of CKD.  Pt was hydrated, 
possibly offending agents were held, and patient was monitored.  
Several days later wtih no improvement of creatinine, decision 
to pursue renal biopsy was made.  Patient underwent renal biopsy 
on ___ while on ASA and Plavix given recently placed bare 
metal stent.  Biopsy was successful and uncomplicated.  The 
following day patient had mild tenderness at biopsy site 
(similar to previous biopsies) and suddenly developed mild 
hematuria and few clots in foley catheter, 3 pt Hct drop noted 
on labs.  Concern for hematoma around transplanted kidney.  
Patient underwent renal ultrasound which showed no hematoma, Hct 
remained stable with no further decline.  Plavix was held for 2 
days in total, ASA was not held. Biopsy results were pending at 
time of discharge but suggestive of worsening fibrosis.  
Immunosuppressants were reduced in dose per renal transplant 
team with plan for close follow up by renal transplant and 
general nephrology to plan for eventual dialysis. 
.

Coronary artery disease remained stable.  Pt was continued on 
antiplatlet agents as above, along with BB, statin, exetimibe.  
Lisinopril was discontinued given ARF, but blood pressure 
remained between 120-150 systolic.  

Symptomatically nausea was resolved at time of discharge. Pt 
otherwise felt well with a good understanding of plan.
